study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Sun et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2025
study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting heterogeneity in major depressive disorder via normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the study objective to dissect heterogeneity in MDD by quantifying individual deviations from a normative model and using these deviations to subtype patients, and to relate subtype patterns to cognition using Neurosynth. This both states the research aims and describes the purpose of applying normative modeling.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Utilizing normative modeling of HC, we quantified individual deviations in brain network degree centrality among MDD patients. Through k-means clustering of these deviation profiles, we identified two clinically meaningful MDD subtypes. Moreover, we employed Neurosynth to analyze the cognitive correlates of these subtypes." ... "we aimed to dissect the heterogeneity in MDD through normative model-driven subtyping of functional brain networks..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Builds a new normative model using healthy controls from REST-meta-MDD. Eligibility and QC criteria are described (age range 18–65; exclude missing demographics; exclude mean FD > 0.2 mm; imaging distortions or signal loss; exclude sites with <10 per group). The original project is cited, and final HC N is reported (822).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The sample data were derived from 1619 participants... 797 MDD... and 822 healthy controls (HC)... These data were obtained from a publicly accessible dataset from the REST-meta-MDD project (Yan et al., 2019) provided by the DIRECT consortium (Chen et al., 2022). ... exclusion criteria ... 1) lack of information on sex, age, or education; 2) age < 18 years or > 65 years; 3) excessive head motion [mean framewise displacement (FD) > 0.2 mm]. ... removed participants with imaging distortions ... did not include the sites with fewer than 10 MDD patients or 10 HC subjects ..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative models map age and sex onto degree centrality. Multi-site effects are handled via hierarchical Bayesian regression, which models site-specific parameters with shared priors to accommodate site variation.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "In this study, age and sex were mapped onto the degree centrality of brain functional networks." ... "To minimize the impact of site-related variability... hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) was employed ... HBR allows for the imposition of a common prior distribution across multiple sites to estimate site-specific yet interrelated means and variances..."
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.location: Sun2025.pdf.md, 2.3 Capturing individual deviations; Fig. 1B caption/context (~lines 84, 92)

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The healthy reference cohort is explicitly from the REST-meta-MDD project by the DIRECT consortium; the project and access information are cited.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "These data were obtained from a publicly accessible dataset from the REST-meta-MDD project (Yan et al., 2019) provided by the DIRECT consortium (Chen et al., 2022)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data from an existing multi-site dataset (REST-meta-MDD) are used; per guidance, acquisition protocol is not required for secondary data.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "These data were obtained from a publicly accessible dataset from the REST-meta-MDD project..."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described with software (DPARSF) and detailed steps: discard first 10 volumes, slice timing correction, realignment, normalization to MNI, nuisance regression (Friston-24, WM, CSF), and bandpass filtering. Graph metrics computed with GRETNA; atlas details provided.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Brain image processing was performed ... using the DPARSF software... The first ten functional volumes were discarded ... corrected for the time shifts ... realigned ... normalized into standard MNI space... nuisance regression ... Friston-24 ... white matter ... CSF ... bandpass filtering 0.01 to 0.10 Hz."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They evaluate generalizability via site-stratified 10-fold cross-validation on the healthy controls before training on all HCs.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "To evaluate the generalizability of the normative models, we first performed normative modeling on the HC using 10-fold cross-validation... Specifically, we stratified the entire HC dataset by site and randomly divided it into 10 folds..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset is reported for validation beyond the REST-meta-MDD HCs; validation described is internal (10-fold CV).
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No statement of applying the normative model to an independent external HC dataset; validation focuses on 10-fold CV within the HC cohort.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The approach is specified: hierarchical Bayesian regression implemented with PCNtoolkit v0.28 to model degree centrality as a function of age and sex per region. Site effects are handled via HBR; training/validation strategy is described.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "To implement normative modeling, we utilized the PCNtoolkit Python package, version 0.28..." ... "Hierarchical Bayesian regression was employed ... to develop a normative model ... for each brain region."
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.location: Sun2025.pdf.md, 2.3 Capturing individual deviations (~lines 84, 92); Fig. 1B description

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Quantitative metrics are reported for the HC cross-validation: standardized mean squared error near 1 and mean squared log-loss near 0, with distribution plots in Fig. S2.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The 10-fold cross-validation performed on the HC revealed the high generalizability ... standardized mean squared error was close to 1 (1.014 ± 0.005), and the mean squared log-loss was close to 0 (0.001 ± 0.004)."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation is used, the paper does not report sample sizes or demographics for each partition (train/validation/test folds). Only total counts and site-stratification are mentioned.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "... we stratified the entire HC dataset by site and randomly divided it into 10 folds..." (no per-fold demographics or sizes provided).

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software/library used and version for normative modeling (PCNtoolkit v0.28) are specified, and data access is stated (REST-meta-MDD open dataset). However, code and trained model availability are not stated; versions for preprocessing tools are not given.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "To implement normative modeling, we utilized the PCNtoolkit Python package, version 0.28 ..." ... "The data used during the present study could be obtained from open dataset (http://rfmri.org/REST-meta-MDD)."
